releases."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Pick an SSH host and a remote directory — that directory becomes a native DSH workspace, and the age"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"nt works **directly on the remote filesystem** through `rw_*` tools (SFTP/exec over a persistent ssh"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"2 pool). No mirror, no sync: the remote is the single source of truth."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"**Zero config since 0.4.0** — once a remote workspace is active, the agent's native `read`/`write`/`"},{"id":"p6s2","text":"edit`/`bash` tools run on the remote host automatically; you never have to teach it a new tool."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"Think of it as the workspace counterpart of an SSH ops toolbox: instead of "run one command over the"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"re", the agent gets a persistent remote project root it can read, edit, build, and test in — like VS"},{"id":"p7s3","text":" Code Remote-SSH, but for your agent."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"## Features"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"- **Remote directory as a native workspace** — a centered picker modal fills the DSH "Add workspace""},{"id":"p9s2","text":" flow: a compact two-card chooser (`LOCAL` / `REMOTE` in English) leads to the local page (OS folder"},{"id":"p9s3","text":" chooser) or a Codex-style remote page (alias-only host dropdown, `~/`-prefilled remote-home path, i"},{"id":"p9s4","text":"nline directory browser with live type-to-filter, optional workspace name).
- **Follows DSH Language"},{"id":"p9s5","text":"** — every picker label, hint, validation message, loading state, confirmation, and fallback message"},{"id":"p9s6","text":" ships in Chinese and English. The active copy follows DSH's global **Settings → Language** preferen"},{"id":"p9s7","text":"ce and updates immediately while the picker is open; no plugin-specific language setting or restart "},{"id":"p9s8","text":"is required.
- **Hosts come from `~/.ssh/config`** — zero configuration: your existing aliases show "},{"id":"p9s9","text":"up automatically (re-read on file change, no restart). Password-auth hosts can be added in the picke"},{"id":"p9s10","text":"r (stored locally, file mode `0600`).
- **Real workspace confinement** — every `rw_*` file path is c"},{"id":"p9s11","text":"onfined to the picked workspace root: `../`, absolute paths outside the root, and symlink escapes (`"},{"id":"p9s12","text":"SYMLINK_ESCAPE` via remote `realpath`) are rejected with structured errors.
- **SSH host key verific"},{"id":"p9s13","text":"ation** — verifies against `~/.ssh/known_hosts` by default (`accept-new`: first-seen keys are record"},{"id":"p9s14","text":"ed), with `strict` and an explicit `off` policy. A changed host key is refused, never silently accep"},{"id":"p9s15","text":"ted.
- **Structured errors** — connection refused / auth failed / timeout / no such path / permissio"},{"id":"p9s16","text":"n denied / outside workspace / host key problems are distinct error codes, so the agent can react co"},{"id":"p9s17","text":"rrectly.
- **Self-healing connections** — the ssh2 pool keepalives (15s × 3) detect dropped connecti"},{"id":"p9s18","text":"ons, and channel/subsystem opens are bounded (`channelOpenTimeoutMs`, default 10s) so a silently dea"},{"id":"p9s19","text":"d connection (half-open TCP) can't hang an operation. An operation that lands on a dead connection i"},{"id":"p9s20","text":"s transparently retried once on a fresh redial — and a **refused channel** counts as dead (proxy fro"},{"id":"p9s21","text":"ntends keep TCP healthy while their backend expires), so a stale pooled connection heals itself inst"},{"id":"p9s22","text":"ead of poisoning every later call.

[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"## Security model"},{"id":"p26s1","text":"- **Workspace confinement** — file tools resolve every path against the workspace root and verify th"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"e *real* path (following symlinks) stays inside. Writes validate the nearest existing ancestor.
- **"},{"id":"p26s3","text":"Host key verification** as described above; host key changes abort the connection with `HOSTKEY_CHAN"},{"id":"p26s4","text":"GED`.
- **Loopback-only HTTP routes** — `/api/dsh-rw/*` refuses non-loopback callers.
- **Secrets** "},{"id":"p26s5","text":"— passwords/passphrases are stored plaintext in `~/.dsh/dsh-rw.json` (mode `0600`, same trust model "},{"id":"p26s6","text":"as `dsh-ssh`); they never appear in tool output, API responses, or error messages. Private keys are "},{"id":"p26s7","text":"only read by ssh2 at connect time.
- **Scope** — giving the plugin a host's credentials lets the age"},{"id":"p26s8","text":"nt run shell commands as that user on that host. Only connect hosts you trust. `rw_delete` performs "},{"id":"p26s9","text":"real remote deletion."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## Known limitations"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"- No ProxyJump / jump-host chains (single-hop only).
- `rw_exec` is one-shot, no interactive PTY.
- "},{"id":"p28s2","text":"File reads are text-oriented (line paging) with a 2 MB cap; large binary transfers are out of scope."},{"id":"p28s3","text":"
- The DSH file tree shows the empty placeholder directory, not remote files — remote browsing happe"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"ns through the picker or the agent."}],"truncated":true}
